control test "a plan with a country can be published" proves that the helper's data is otherwise
valid, and Strapi does not reject `[]` for a non-required repeatable (F01 evidence). So removing
the middleware turns the test red, even without a message assertion. The real gap is the other
branches of `plan-coverages.ts:18-25`:
- `publish` of an existing draft that has no coverages. This is the editor's normal path: save a
  draft, then publish.
- `update` with `status: 'published'` and no `coverages` in `data`, which goes through the draft
  lookup.

No test covers either. A mutation that drops `context.action === 'publish' ||` or the draft
lookup goes unnoticed. If F01 is fixed through the schema, a single "publish an existing draft
with no coverage is refused" test still pins the behaviour. Asserting the Spanish message
(`'Un plan publicado necesita al menos una cobertura.'`) would also make each test fail for the
right reason.

### US-02-R1-F03 — The money formatter's options are untyped

`money-format.ts:15-21` casts the whole object through `unknown`, so a typo such as
`maximumFractionDigit: 0` or `style: 'curency'` would compile. The comment's reasoning is right:
the ES2022 typings lack `'always'`. But the fix is available. With
`tsc --target ES2022 --lib ES2022,ES2023.Intl`, `useGrouping: 'always'` type-checks with no

property would also keep the rest of the object checked. AC-06 is met; this is maintainability
only.

   checked by nobody. A mechanical check (for example, a recorded expected count that the script
   compares, or a `trace.sh`/gate step that runs the log scan against a baseline) would make it

`e266d9a test(backend): remove probe plans after each test…` changed `plan-rules.test.ts` after

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the Playwright e2e suite against a running stack, with the documented defaults.
# Exists so that nobody (human or agent) has to rebuild the env line by hand: a hand-built
# `env $VARS` line silently broke the gate once (zsh does not word-split unquoted variables).

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/frontend"

### 7.1 `plan` collection type (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string, required | `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`. Unique per country (Document Service middleware, US-02-Q-05). Not shown to users. |
| `name` | string, required | Spanish, non-empty. |
| `shortDescription` | string, required, `maxLength: 200` | Spanish, non-empty. |
| `basePrice` | integer, required, `min: 1` | Annual, whole units of the country's currency (US-02-Q-06, Q-08). |
| `coverages` | repeatable component `plan.coverage`, `min: 1` | Order as edited. |
| `benefits` | repeatable component `plan.benefit` | Zero or more. Order as edited. |
| `sortOrder` | integer, required | Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `isRecommended` | boolean, default `false` | US-02-Q-09. |
| `isActive` | boolean, default `true` | US-02-Q-10. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

No `currency` attribute, subject to US-02-Q-02.

Components: `plan.coverage` and `plan.benefit`, each with one attribute `label` (string, required,
Spanish).

### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping

Request (one per page load, through the proxy, published content only, ADR-0002):

```
GET /api/plans?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&filters[isActive][$eq]=true
  &fields[0]=key&fields[1]=name&fields[2]=shortDescription&fields[3]=basePrice
  &fields[4]=sortOrder&fields[5]=isRecommended&fields[6]=isActive
  &populate[coverages][fields][0]=label&populate[benefits][fields][0]=label
  &sort[0]=sortOrder:asc&sort[1]=key:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100
```

Example response item (illustrative; Strapi adds `id`, `documentId`, component `id` and `meta`,
which the parser ignores):

```json
{ "id": 7, "documentId": "…", "key": "clasico", "name": "Plan Clásico",
  "shortDescription": "Cubre los daños a terceros y la pérdida total de tu vehículo.",
  "basePrice": 1400000, "sortOrder": 20, "isRecommended": true, "isActive": true,
  "coverages": [ { "id": 31, "label": "Pérdida total por daños" } ],
  "benefits": [ { "id": 52, "label": "Asistencia en carretera 24/7" } ] }
```

### US-02-R2-F01 — The spec's §7.1 does not reflect `required` on `coverages`

**Does the new draft rule conflict with spec v0.1?** No.
- The spec talks about drafts only as "not shown" or "never readable anonymously" (BR-02, BR-06,
  AC-08, AC-19). It sets no rule for what a draft may hold.

`required`, `min: 1`; a draft may hold `[]`, but `coverages` must be sent on create").

only when the editor removes that row.

The reviewer removed `"required": true` from `coverages` in
`backend/src/api/plan/content-types/plan/schema.json` (uncommitted), ran the plan tests, and
restored the file with `git checkout --`. `git status` was clean afterwards. Red tests:

- `US-02-AC-09 refuses to publish a plan with no coverage (min 1)`
- `US-02-AC-09 refuses to publish an existing draft that has no coverages, and no published version appears`
- `US-02-AC-09 refuses to create a draft with coverages unset (no draft without a list); …`
- `US-02-AC-09 refuses to publish a draft whose coverages an editor emptied after saving it valid`
- `US-02-AC-09 refuses to update a published plan so that it has no coverages, and the published coverages stay`

The control test (`a draft with coverages publishes, and a published plan can be updated with
other coverages`) stays green, so the red tests fail because of the rule and not because the
helper data is invalid. This matches the Strapi 5.63 validator
(`@strapi/core/dist/services/entity-validator/index.js`):
- `addMinMax` (lines 36-44) applies `min` only when the attribute is `required` or the array is
  non-empty;
- repeatables call it only when `!options.isDraft` (lines 105-110);
- `addDefault` (lines 60-74) defaults a non-required repeatable to `[]` on creation, and a
  required one to `undefined`, which `notNil()` (lines 45-58) rejects even on a draft.

still accepted.

200), before the stack was removed with `down -v`.

| Step | Variant A: new plan, coverage row left as the admin pre-fills it | Variant B: the pre-filled coverage row deleted (`coverages (0)*`) |
|---|---|---|
| Payload of "Save" | `coverages: [{ __temp_key__ }]`: one blank row | `coverages: []` |
| Save the draft | 201; the draft holds `[{ label: null }]` | 201; the draft holds `[]` |

| Published version afterwards | none | none |

its own client-side message first, so this is no finding.
